tasks.goal: Implement the v1.2 separation between live cleanup completeness and durable controller-death recovery completeness on top of reviewed draft a9d6e00 per design/nested-registry-live-cleanup-v1.2.md. Keep the persisted WorkerLease bounded, but stop letting persistence bounds for groups or ungrouped fallback identities fail a live cleanup when a validated current process-table snapshot can enumerate all currently reachable groups up to the existing 8192-row cap. During live cleanup, build a current in-memory group view independent of the 16-group lease persistence cap; use guarded negative-pgid cleanup for every current external group with fresh exact pid===pgid leader and membership proof, and exact-pid fallback only for truly ungrouped targets. Persist and report truncation separately as durable-recovery completeness. Mark live cleanup failed only for incomplete current inspection, unsafe identity/group proof, over-bound live ungrouped targets, signal failure or residual processes. A truncated persisted registry with a complete live cleanup may produce a released lease whose controller-death recovery evidence is explicitly truncated/needs_human; it must not reject an otherwise successful Worker. Preserve the reviewed exact leader identity, self/own-group guards, status projection, parser compatibility and no-broad-scan rules. Add real POSIX tests with more than 16 external groups and a 512-member group proving live cleanup succeeds and no residual remains while the durable registry is truncated, followed by recover-workers reporting needs_human with no signal from that truncated lease. Add tests that incomplete live inspection still fails closed, unsafe/reused leaders remain untouched and existing exact-fallback/lease/Supervisor behavior remains green. Do not change TaskContract, RunManifest acceptance, verifier timeouts, RuntimeManager, Windows or cross-host behavior.
nonGoals: Do not make the lease or process scan unbounded.
Do not weaken exact group leader or membership guards.
Do not make controller-death recovery act on truncated evidence.
Do not change verifier timeout policy in this task.
Do not claim Windows, cross-host or OS write sandbox support.
Do not automatically accept or merge prior blocked runs.
deliverables: Separate live cleanup completeness from durable recovery completeness in code, status projection and tests.
Real POSIX evidence for more than 16 external groups, including a 512-member group, with zero residual processes.
Truncated durable lease recovery that reports needs_human without signalling.
forbidden: Do not increase the durable lease without a new bounded schema and migration decision.
Do not treat a group id alone as ownership after controller death.
Do not make a truncated durable registry reject a proven complete live cleanup.
Do not use process names, ports or broad process scans as kill authority.
